claim: Failure to pay marking duties may give rise to reverse false claims liability under the False Claims Act, and an importer who knowingly fails to disclose to Customs and Border Protection that its goods are unmarked or improperly marked, in violation of its affirmative disclosure obligation under 19 U.S.C. § 1484(a)(1), is liable under the FCA without having made any express false statement to the government.
initial_reasoning: 41 F.4th 83 is the Supreme Court decision in United States v. United States Customs and Border Protection, which held that an importer who knowingly fails to disclose unmarked or improperly marked goods to CBP can be liable under the False Claims Act for reverse false claims liability, even without an express false statement, because the affirmative disclosure obligation under 19 U.S.C. § 1484(a)(1) is violated.
